name: Placard
oneLiner: A mid-century civic poster: flat mustard and teal fields, a geometric megaphone, evidence set loud and ruled.
concept:
The other directions ask the reader to trust a document: a ledger, a broadsheet, a signed note, a record card. Placard asks them to trust a sign. It borrows the lineage of the WPA, Swiss and Bauhaus civic poster, where a public message had to be read from across a street: two flat fields, one object, one line, one rule. The hero is a poster pinned to a white wall. A deep teal field carries the whole promise in three ruled lines, '$10,000 a month. Kept, not lost. Be heard.', the offer, the promise and the mission in the order a placard is read. A mustard field carries the megaphone rebuilt as pure geometry: an ink circle, a teal wedge with an ink rim, and three tomato bars radiating from the mouth through a single halftone disc. Google's 5% rule sits on the poster itself as a tomato badge under the words 'Google's rule', because a rule you can read from across the room is a rule you stop being afraid of.

Everything that proves the claim is set as poster copy: short, loud, ruled. Below the poster, a white imprint strip inside 4px ink rules carries the three figures in numbered circles (100% acquisition guarantee, 780+ nonprofit clients, $48M+ managed), Michelle Hurtado's endorsement under a teal kicker giving her Google title, and the eight client names as tracked capitals between mustard squares. There are no gradients, no shadows, no rounded cards and no photography in the hero; the only curve on the page is a circle. Type does the rest: Archivo Black uppercase at 50 and 88px against Archivo body at 17 and 12px, so the scale jump itself reads as volume. The register is optimistic civic confidence, the tone of a public-works poster rather than a marketing site, which is exactly the calm, forwardable authority a tired executive director wants to put in front of a board.
distinctFrom: It is the only direction whose first impression is two saturated flat fields and a geometric object rather than a paper, newsprint, white or blue-wall ground with type and evidence laid on it.
bullets: Flat mustard and teal fields, ink type, one tomato badge.
The megaphone rebuilt from a circle, a wedge and three bars.
Evidence set like poster copy: numbered circles, heavy rules, capitals.
rightFor: A leadership team ready to own a bold public identity and look like the category leader, not another blue agency.
needs: Approve retiring the blue as primary
Redraw the mark as poster geometry
Fund a Webflow poster component kit

palette.note: Plain white outside the poster blocks: the masthead, the imprint strip and every page below the fold. The poster is a figure on a wall, never a full-bleed wash.

First dominant field: the object panel, the primary button on teal, the numbered circles, the client-roll squares, the eyebrow rule and the 'Be heard.' line. Ink on it measures 9.3:1; it never carries white or tomato text.
Second dominant field: the copy panel, the horn of the megaphone, and the kicker colour on white (5.8:1). Only white text sits on it; ink on teal fails (3.0:1) and is never used.

Used sparingly: the three sound bars, the 5% badge disc and the current-page underline. White numerals on it pass only at large size (4.3:1), so the badge figure is 30px Archivo Black (24px on phone); never a body-text colour and never placed on teal.
Reserved for any tomato under 24px on white below the fold, such as a policy callout or the 5% line label on a chart (5.3:1). Not used in the hero.
Headlines on mustard and white, all rules (2 to 4px), the megaphone circle and rim, the nav button fill, the focus ring on light grounds. Near-black, never pure.
The 'Among 780+ clients' kicker and secondary labels on white only (8.0:1).
Ink dots on a 9px pitch from one CSS radial-gradient, clipped to a single 340px disc behind the megaphone mouth. The only texture in the system; it appears once per page and never under text.

typography.display: Archivo Black (Google Fonts, single 400 weight): every headline, the figures in the imprint strip, the 5% badge numeral, the wordmark and the numbered circles. Always uppercase at display sizes via CSS text-transform; never used below 11px (the circle numerals) and never for running text.
typography.body: Archivo (Google Fonts, 400 to 700): 400 for body and the hero sub, 600 for nav links, labels and the badge sentence, 700 for buttons, kickers, the eyebrow and the client roll. Labels are uppercase with .06 to .12em tracking; the sub and the quote are sentence case. Both families load from fonts.googleapis.com only.
typography.scaleNotes: Desktop h1 in three ruled lines: '$10,000 a month.' and 'Kept, not lost.' at 50px / .92, 'Be heard.' at 88px / .9 in mustard (3.1:1 on teal, large text only), all Archivo Black uppercase at -0.01em, measured at 509 / 461 / 528px inside a 540px column so no line can wrap. Phone h1 31 / 31 / 52px (313 / 284 / 311px in a 350px column). Sub 17px / 1.5 on desktop at max-width 490px, 16px on phone, white on teal. Imprint figures 32px Archivo Black over 12px uppercase labels (22px over 11px on phone); badge numeral 30px (24px on phone) with an 11px kicker and a 13px sentence (12px on phone). Buttons 56px on desktop (44px in the nav, 52px on phone, 36px in the phone nav), 15px Archivo 700 uppercase at .06em, square corners, 2px keyline in the fill colour so the boundary never depends on fill alone. Kickers, imprint and the roll label 11px, which is the floor; nothing is set smaller. Rules: 4px ink to frame the imprint strip, 3px under the masthead and above the poster imprint, 2px inside strips. Spacing on an 8px base: nav 72, gap 20, poster 552 (teal 640 / mustard 464), gap 20, imprint strip 161, bottom pad 24, whole frame 849px.

layout:
- Grid: 1200px container with a 48px outer margin, so every block is 1104 wide and the poster sits inside a white wall; poster panels 640 teal / 464 mustard; 8px rhythm; sections are framed by 4px ink rules and numbered circles instead of cards, and the object appears at most three times per page (hero, 'one of nine' band, footer mark).
- 00 Masthead (72px, white, 3px ink rule): the geometric mini-mark (ink circle, teal wedge, three tomato bars at 36px) + NONPROFIT MEGAPHONE in Archivo Black; Services, Our work, Happy clients, Team, Blog with a 3px tomato underline on the current page; 'Get a free quote' as an underlined link to the existing landing page; 'Book a free call' as an ink block button.
- 01 Poster (552px): teal copy panel with a mustard-ruled eyebrow 'Google search ads for nonprofits · $10,000 a month, free', the three-line h1, a four-line sub (acquire, keep above 5%, run weekly, be found first), a mustard 'Book a free call' beside a white-outline 'Am I eligible?', and the guarantee footer above a 2px rule: a circle portrait of Amber Snow, 'Our guarantee is a person, not a policy', the $25 promise and 'Read the guarantee'. Mustard object panel with the 5% badge (88px tomato disc, 'Google's rule' kicker, the two-missed-months sentence), the geometric megaphone over one halftone disc, and a ruled imprint at bottom right: 'One of nine inaugural Google Ad Grants Certified Professional agencies · 60+ person team'.
- 02 Imprint strip (white, 4px rules top and bottom): three cells divided by 2px rules, each a mustard numbered circle beside 100% / 780+ / $48M+ in Archivo Black with an uppercase label (Acquisition guarantee, Nonprofit clients, Ad spend managed); a fourth cell with Michelle Hurtado's name and title as a teal kicker over her quote at 17px; then a 2px rule and the client roll, 'Among 780+ clients' followed by UNCF, Scouting America, COPD Foundation, YWCA Chicago, Earthwatch, Solar Sister, AAU, JFCS as tracked capitals between mustard squares.
- 03 The rules, as a poster series: three flat blocks (mustard, teal, ink) each with a numbered circle, one rule Google enforces (5% click-through rate, conversion tracking, monthly account activity) in short capitals, what happens when it is missed, and what NPM does about it; sourced to Google's policy page with a date.
- 04 Eligibility placard: a white block inside a 4px ink frame with three yes/no questions (organisation type, country, working website) as square 24px checkboxes, and an honest 'not eligible, and why' outcome for hospitals, schools and governments quoting Google's definition; no rep, no form submission.
- 05 Outcomes board: the published case studies as a ruled table (organisation, cause, what changed, period, source) with numbered circles down the left edge and no cards; every row opens a case file and a forwardable PDF; filter chips are square, ink-outlined, 44px tall.
- 06 Services: the seven services (Ad Grant management, Website SEO, Content creation, VisitorEmail, Google Remarketing, Microsoft Advertising, Spanish ad creation) as one ruled list on mustard, with a flat monthly fee statement if leadership approves publishing it, never a percentage of spend; price is a screening question so it sits before the team.
- 07 One of nine (teal band, contained inside the 48px margin): the inaugural certification, Google's 8x conversion-value stat for certified-managed grantees with its source, the Google Partner badge inside its clear space, Inc. 5000 x4 as four numbered circles; the megaphone object at low white opacity behind.
- 08 The team, named: 60+ people as flat two-colour portrait crops (photographs posterised to ink on mustard) in a ruled grid with names, roles and 'Nonprofits I support'; copy stating who the prospect's named point of contact will be.
- 09 Reporting, shown: a real monthly report redrawn as a ruled poster panel (utilisation against the $10,000 cap, click-through rate against the 5% floor drawn as a tomato rule, compliance ticks as filled squares), redactions as solid ink blocks, signed by a named account lead with the month.
- 10 Guarantee band (ink): the $25 CEO guarantee in 64px Archivo Black mustard, Amber Snow named and pictured as a circle portrait, 'a person, not a policy', one mustard button.
- 11 FAQ as a ruled definition list (why pay for something free; will it raise money, answered honestly; who is on my account; what if we get suspended; how long to acquire), each with a dated source line where a policy is cited.
- 12 Final CTA: the hero action pair repeated on teal plus 'See a real account report' as an underlined link to a redacted PDF.
- 13 Footer (white, 2px rules): four columns, newsletter, address, socials, client login; the mini-mark once; print stylesheet turns every field to white with ink rules.
imagery: A poster system, not an illustration system. First, the geometric megaphone: one inline SVG built from three primitives, a circle (ink, r 58), a wedge (teal, 56 wide at the mouthpiece, 224 wide at the mouth, 250 long at 30 degrees) with an ink rim 22 deep, and three tomato bars 20 wide radiating from a point 62 beyond the rim at -58, -30 and -2 degrees, over a single halftone disc; the same file is cropped to its bounding box for the phone band and reduced to 36px for the masthead mark, so the whole identity is three shapes and four colours that anyone can redraw with a ruler and a compass. Second, flat two-colour portraits: team and CEO photographs posterised to ink on mustard (or white on teal) with hard edges and no gradients, in circles for the hero guarantee and in ruled rectangles for the team grid; the mockups carry a labelled circle placeholder until the shoot. Third, real screens as poster panels: the monthly report and the Ad Grants account view redrawn flat with 2px rules, ink redaction blocks and a tomato 5% line, never screenshots with drop shadows. Fourth, the client roll as tracked Archivo capitals between mustard squares, so no logo licensing is needed. Icons are solid geometric glyphs (square, circle, wedge, bar) with a 2px minimum stroke and no outlines. Charts: white ground, 2px ink axes, mustard and teal series, a tomato rule for Google's 5% floor wherever click-through rate is charted, unit and period on every chart, sourced footnote beneath. The halftone dot texture appears once per page and never under text. No stock photography; beneficiary photography only inside consented case files, never as decoration.
motion: Almost none, and none of it required. 1. Poster load (pure CSS, shipped in both mockups): the three tomato bars scale out from the megaphone mouth with a 90ms stagger over 450ms, then the 5% badge and the halftone disc fade in behind them; every word is readable from frame one and the whole sequence is under 600ms. 2. Buttons swap fills on hover with no transition, like a stamped state change: mustard to white on teal, ink to white on white, the outline button fills white with teal text. 3. Nav links gain their ink underline instantly; the current page keeps its tomato underline. 4. Below the fold, optional and separately budgeted: section frames draw from the left on scroll and numbered circles stamp in (scale .8 to 1 over 200ms), native scroll only, no library over 50kB, no Lenis. 5. Every keyframe lives inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference, so reduced-motion users get the finished poster with zero animation. Never: parallax, marquees, autoplaying video, kinetic type, hover lifts, shadows or looping motion.
mobile: The 390px hero is a stacked poster, not the desktop squeezed. Masthead (56px, 3px ink rule): the 28px geometric mark beside a two-line NONPROFIT / MEGAPHONE at 11px Archivo Black, a 36px ink 'Book a call' button and a 40px menu button with aria-expanded. Then a full-bleed mustard band (176px) with the megaphone cropped from the desktop SVG at 198px wide on the left and the 5% badge on the right (56px tomato disc, 24px numeral, 'Google's rule' kicker, a three-line sentence), the halftone disc behind the bars. Then the teal copy block (20px gutters): the two-line eyebrow, h1 at 31 / 31 / 52px, a five-line sub at 16px, a full-width 52px mustard 'Book a free call' and a full-width 48px white-outline 'Am I eligible?' button; measured, the primary sits at 576px and the eligibility button at 638px, both inside the 760px fold. One trust element follows on white between 4px rules: Michelle Hurtado's title as a teal kicker, her quote at 16px, and a three-cell ruled stat row with 24px numbered circles (100%, 780+, $48M+). Below the fold the imprint strip stacks, the rules series becomes three full-width blocks, the eligibility placard keeps its square checkboxes at 44px, the outcomes board becomes ruled rows with the same five fields, and the team grid goes to two columns. Tap targets 44px minimum; the halftone keeps its 9px pitch; nothing scrolls horizontally at 390.
a11y: Target WCAG 2.2 AA, measured on the actual grounds. White on teal 5.8:1 (hero eyebrow, sub, guarantee line, outline button, kicker); ink on mustard 9.3:1 (badge kicker and sentence, imprint, primary button label, numbered circles); ink on white 17.4:1; #4D4D4D secondary on white 8.0:1; teal kicker on white 5.8:1. Mustard 'Be heard.' on teal is 3.1:1 and is used only at 88px (52px on phone), which clears the 3:1 large-text threshold; it is the sole mustard-on-teal text in the system. White numeral on tomato is 4.3:1 at 30px and 24px Archivo Black, large text only; tomato is never used for text under 24px, and #C43A1F (5.3:1 on white) is the small-text tomato. Non-text contrast: the mustard button on teal 3.1:1 and the white outline 5.8:1, and every button carries a 2px keyline so its boundary never depends on fill alone. Frame: desktop 849px (masthead 72, gap 20, poster 552, gap 20, imprint 161, pad 24) with the copy panel measured at exactly its 552px; phone primary CTA at 576px and eligibility button at 638px inside a 760px fold; nothing overflows 1200 or 390. Type floor 11px (kickers, imprint, circle numerals), 12px labels, 13px badge sentence and guarantee, 15 to 17px everything else. Semantics: the megaphone is an aria-hidden decorative SVG inside a figure whose visually hidden figcaption states what it shows and repeats Google's rule; the 5% badge is real DOM text, read as 'five percent' with no ARIA needed; every figure, name and the quote are real DOM text in reading order; the circle numerals are aria-hidden so screen readers hear the figures without stray digits; the portrait placeholder carries role='img' with a label; the menu button has aria-expanded. Focus: a 3px solid outline offset 3px, ink on white and mustard, white on teal, visible on every ground. Motion: all keyframes inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference; the load sequence is under 600ms and nothing loops. Headings are uppercase via CSS text-transform, so assistive technology receives sentence case. Pointer targets 44px on touch. Print stylesheet flattens fields to white with ink rules.

heroCopy.eyebrow: Google search ads for nonprofits · $10,000 a month, free
heroCopy.headline: $10,000 a month. Kept, not lost. Be heard.
heroCopy.sub: Google gives eligible nonprofits $10,000 a month in search ads. We get it for you, guaranteed, keep it above Google's 5% click-through floor, and run it every week so the people searching for your cause find you first.

signatureMoments: The two-field poster: a teal copy panel and a mustard object panel abutting inside a white margin, so the first screen is a sign on a wall rather than a page with a hero on it.

The geometric megaphone: an ink circle, a teal wedge with an ink rim and three tomato bars over one halftone disc; the same three shapes become the 36px masthead mark and the phone band, so the identity is drawable by anyone with a ruler and a compass.
The 5% badge: Google's deactivation rule set as a tomato disc under the words 'Google's rule', on the poster itself, turning the buyer's private fear into a public, readable fact.
The three-line headline: '$10,000 a month. Kept, not lost. Be heard.', with the last line at 88px in mustard, the offer, the promise and the mission in the reading order of a placard.

The imprint strip: 100% / 780+ / $48M+ in numbered circles, the Head of Ad Grants quote under a teal kicker, and the client roll in capitals between mustard squares, all inside 4px ink rules, evidence set like the small print at the foot of a poster.
dependencies: Approve retiring the electric blue as the primary colour: mustard and teal become the brand fields and the mark is redrawn as the circle-wedge-bars geometry, because the current megaphone icon does not survive as-is.
Sign off the headline '$10,000 a month. Kept, not lost. Be heard.' and the badge sentence about deactivation after two missed months against Google's current policy wording, with a dated source.
Approve the guarantee copy: Amber Snow named and pictured, 'Our guarantee is a person, not a policy', the $25 mechanism and a real 'Read the guarantee' destination.

Fund a portrait treatment: posterised two-colour crops of Amber Snow and the team (a half-day shoot plus retouching to a fixed ink-on-mustard recipe); the mockups ship a labelled circle placeholder until then.
Webflow build with a locked component kit (field block, numbered circle, ruled strip, badge, poster button) and a style page so editors cannot introduce radii, shadows, gradients or a fourth colour.
risks: Mustard and teal are a departure from the blue that 780 clients recognise; the masthead, buttons and every page below the fold must carry the new fields consistently or the site splits into two brands. Approve the palette before build, not after.

A poster register can tip into shouting. The discipline is one badge, three bars, one halftone disc and no tomato text; if editors add red headlines or a second badge it becomes a sale flyer. Lock the tokens and the SVG.

Flat fields leave less room for long copy; the hero sub is capped at four lines and every section below the fold is written as short ruled statements, which needs a copy pass NPM may not have budgeted.

Two of the strongest colour moves (mustard on teal, white on tomato) pass only at large sizes; any editor who shrinks them breaks AA. The style page must state the size floors and the build should enforce them with locked classes.
references: WPA Federal Art Project posters (1936 to 1943): flat fields, one object, one rule, public-service tone
Swiss International Style posters (Josef Müller-Brockmann, Armin Hofmann): grid, scale contrast, geometry as image
Bauhaus and Herbert Bayer: circle, wedge and bar as a complete visual vocabulary
The National Park Service poster series: civic optimism without stock photography
Community Boost (the direct competitor): the blue, rounded, gradient category look this direction leaves behind
